text:
# Prescriptive lessons - mick-goodrick x almanac-vol-1

The Almanac of Voice-Leading for Guitar is a purely tabular reference work - Goodrick provides no prose explanations, only dense catalog grids of voicings, cycles, and MSRP positions. Every lesson below is therefore extracted by inference from the structural logic of the catalog itself: how the tables are organized, which chord qualities appear in which parent scales, and what the cycling sequences imply about voice-leading behavior.

---

## maj7

Maj7 chords appear as tonic (Cmaj7, Fmaj7) in C major and as bVI (Abmaj7) in C harmonic minor, making them the most contextually stable entries in the catalog. The Close/Spread pairing and the full MSRP matrix together generate the complete voice-leading surface for this quality across all six cycles.

- **voicing-density-pairing** - Practice Cmaj7 and Fmaj7 in both Close and Spread voicings across every cycle as paired entries; observe which upper voice carries the common tone as density shifts. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **voice-leading-through-cycle-2** - Stepwise root motion produces the tightest upper-voice motion of any cycle; use the Intervallic layer to confirm no voice exceeds a major second. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **voice-leading-through-cycle-5** - Cmaj7 to Fmaj7 in Cycle 5 mimics dominant-resolution root motion; the major seventh resolves or is retained as a common tone - consult the Functional layer. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **msrp-top-voice-policy** - All four MSRP positions (Root/3/5/7 on top) yield distinct voicing shapes; cycle all four across Cycles 2-7 to build the complete voice-leading matrix. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **parent-scale-context-harmonic-minor** - Abmaj7 as bVI in C harmonic minor functions as tonic-substitute or pre-dominant; keep its function distinct from Cmaj7's unambiguous tonic role in C major. [ch.1 pp.12-189]

---

## min7

Min7 chords carry dual harmonic weight as ii chords (Dmin7 in C major) and as tonic stand-ins in modal contexts, making Cycle 5 and Cycle 3 the highest-priority practice cycles for this quality. The melodic minor parent scale introduces min-maj7 as a competing voicing option that reshapes the MSRP top-voice hierarchy.

- **voicing-density-pairing** - Drill Dmin7 in both Close and Spread across all cycles; note that Spread voicings thin the minor-third stack and shift common-tone placement. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **voice-leading-through-cycle-5** - Dmin7 to G7 is the canonical ii-V motion; use this cycle as the primary testing ground for min7 upper-voice resolution behavior. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **voice-leading-through-cycle-3** - Minor-third root motion between min7 chords shares common tones across all upper voices; verify that the Intervallic layer shows minimal displacement. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **msrp-top-voice-policy** - Four MSRP positions produce four independent melodic lines across the ii-V-I sequence; practice each top-voice choice through Cycle 5 as a complete phrase. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **parent-scale-context-melodic-minor** - Min7 built on the first degree of melodic minor competes with min-maj7; track which scale degree is in use before assigning a quality to any minor tonic. [ch.1 pp.12-189]

---

## dom7

Dom7 is the most functionally loaded quality in the catalog - it generates tritone tension, supports substitution, appears in both major and harmonic-minor contexts, and is the native chord of Cycle 5. The MSRP choice of 7-on-top vs. 3-on-top controls whether the resolution voice is the leading tone or the chordal seventh.

- **voicing-density-pairing** - Close voicings concentrate the tritone between adjacent strings; Spread voicings distribute it, altering perceived tension - practice both across every cycle to internalize the density-to-function relationship. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **voice-leading-through-cycle-5** - Cycle 5 is the home cycle for dom7; trace the tritone resolution (7->3, 3->7) explicitly in each upper-voice line and confirm against the Functional layer. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **voice-leading-through-cycle-2** - Stepwise dominant motion (chromatic parallel dominants) suspends tritone resolution; use the Intervallic layer to log each half-step voice displacement. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **msrp-top-voice-policy** - 7-on-top places the chordal seventh as melody, resolving down by step; 3-on-top places the leading tone as melody, resolving up - practice both resolutions through a ii-V-I in every key. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **parent-scale-context-harmonic-minor** - V7 in C harmonic minor (G7) contains the raised seventh of the scale; mark this entry separately from the C-major G7 and compare upper-voice approach notes. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **functional-voice-leading-substitution** - Tritone substitutes (Db7 for G7) share the same tritone pair with inverted resolution direction; the catalog's Functional layer maps both to the same functional slot - cross-reference both entries. [ch.1 pp.12-189]

---

## min7b5

Min7b5 (half-diminished) occupies the vii position in major and the ii position in harmonic/melodic minor, making its Cycle 5 behavior (iimin7b5-V7-i) its most important functional application. The flattened fifth creates an asymmetric voicing shape that behaves differently in Close vs. Spread density.

- **voicing-density-pairing** - The b5 interval sits inside the Close voicing stack in a way that Spread voicings expose differently on the fretboard; practice both to internalize the fingerboard geometry of the diminished interval. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **voice-leading-through-cycle-5** - iimin7b5 to V7 in minor is the defining ii-V context; use the Functional layer to track whether the b5 resolves down by half-step to the root of V7 or is retained. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **parent-scale-context-melodic-minor** - Min7b5 built on the sixth degree of melodic minor (locrian #2) has a natural second rather than b2; mark this entry separately from the harmonic-minor half-diminished and compare approach tones. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **msrp-top-voice-policy** - With b5 as a potential top voice, the MSRP matrix includes an acoustically tense melodic option; practice 5-on-top entries to build comfort resolving the dissonance in melody position. [ch.1 pp.12-189]

---

## dim7

Dim7 is the only fully symmetric quality in the catalog - its inversional equivalence means four chord names map to three unique voicing shapes, and Cycle 3 (minor-third root motion) produces literal zero net displacement. Its primary functional role is as a rootless V7b9.

- **voicing-density-pairing** - Because all inversions are enharmonically equivalent, Close and Spread density is the primary differentiator between dim7 voicings; map each density to its enharmonic alias before practicing cycles. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **voice-leading-through-cycle-3** - Minor-third root motion between dim7 chords is a closed system: the voicing returns to its origin after four moves - use this cycle explicitly to demonstrate the symmetry rather than for genuine voice-leading practice. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **functional-voice-leading-substitution** - Viio7 functions as V7b9 with the root omitted; cross-reference the dim7 catalog entries with the dom7 V7b9 entries and confirm the Functional layer assigns identical resolution targets. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **parent-scale-context-harmonic-minor** - Harmonic minor is the only diatonic source of dim7 in the catalog (built on vii); flag this exclusive parent-scale relationship and use it to distinguish dim7 from min7b5 in minor-key ii-V writing. [ch.1 pp.12-189]

---

## min-maj7

Min-maj7 is the tonic chord of melodic minor and the most harmonically unstable-sounding tonic in the catalog - the natural seventh creates an unresolved leading tone against a minor third. Its Cycle 5 and MSRP behaviors are critical for navigating melodic minor ii-V-i progressions.

- **voicing-density-pairing** - The major seventh sitting above a minor third is especially compressed in Close voicing; Spread voicings redistribute the interval and reduce the acoustic tension - practice both before committing to a register preference. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **voice-leading-through-cycle-5** - As tonic in melodic minor, min-maj7 receives resolution from the V7 chord; track whether the major seventh appears in the bass or an upper voice and how it connects to the preceding dominant. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **msrp-top-voice-policy** - 7-on-top places the leading tone as melody on the tonic chord, a particularly striking color; practice all four MSRP positions and note the dramatic difference in stability between maj7-on-top and root-on-top. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **parent-scale-context-melodic-minor** - Min-maj7 is diatonic only to melodic minor as a tonic chord; any other appearance is a borrowed or chromatic event - annotate the parent scale explicitly on every min-maj7 catalog entry used. [ch.1 pp.12-189]

---

## aug-maj7

Aug-maj7 is the tonic chord of harmonic minor - the raised fifth creates an augmented triad over the major seventh, producing a sound that is simultaneously stable (tonic function) and acoustically vivid (augmented fifth). Its shared common tones with min-maj7 make it a key substitution resource.

- **voicing-density-pairing** - The augmented fifth spreads unusually across the fretboard in Close voicing; Spread voicings normalize the interval spacing and are often more playable - map both before selecting a default position. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **parent-scale-context-harmonic-minor** - Aug-maj7 is diatonic only to harmonic minor as a tonic chord; mark this exclusive parentage in the catalog and use it to identify harmonic-minor key centers by ear. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **functional-voice-leading-substitution** - Aug-maj7 and min-maj7 share three common tones (root, minor third, major seventh); cross-reference both catalog entries on the Functional layer to map the one-note difference and its voice-leading implications. [ch.1 pp.12-189]

---

## aug-triad

The augmented triad is fully symmetric under major-third root motion, making it - like the dim7 - a closed system in Cycle 3. It appears diatonically in melodic minor and is the harmonic skeleton of the aug-maj7 and aug7 chord families.

- **voicing-density-pairing** - Because aug triads have only three distinct pitch classes, Close and Spread voicings are the primary distinguishing variable; practice both densities and note that each produces only three unique shapes regardless of inversion. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **voice-leading-through-cycle-3** - Major-third root motion between aug triads returns to the origin after three moves - zero net displacement, analogous to dim7 in Cycle 3 - use this cycle to demonstrate the symmetry explicitly. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **parent-scale-context-melodic-minor** - The aug triad built on the third degree of melodic minor is the only diatonic aug triad in the catalog's parent-scale system; flag this and use it to locate aug-triad entries within the melodic minor section. [ch.1 pp.12-189]

---

## maj-triad

The major triad has only three distinct pitches and therefore only three MSRP positions (Root/3/5 on top); its catalog entries are the most compact of any quality. Cycle 6 (major-sixth / relative-minor root motion) is its most characteristic cycle because it connects tonic major to its relative minor with common-tone efficiency.

- **voicing-density-pairing** - With only three voices, Close and Spread produce a marked difference in register and string-set; practice both and treat each as a distinct timbre rather than a voicing variant of the same object. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **voice-leading-through-cycle-6** - Major-sixth root motion connects C major to A minor sharing two common tones; use this cycle to practice parallel major-to-relative-minor motion and observe which voice moves by step. [ch.1 pp.12-189]

---

## min-triad

The minor triad shares the three-voice MSRP structure of the major triad but carries the functional weight of ii in minor-key Cycle 5 progressions. Its harmonic-minor parent-scale context (built on iv) makes it essential for minor ii-V construction even without the seventh.

- **voicing-density-pairing** - Close vs. Spread on a minor triad shifts the minor third between adjacent or separated string groups; practice both and identify which density produces the darker timbre on your specific guitar. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **voice-leading-through-cycle-5** - ii minor triad to V in a minor key produces a functional ii-V without the added seventh; use the Functional layer to confirm the b3 resolution target and compare to the full min7b5-V7 entry. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **parent-scale-context-harmonic-minor** - The iv minor triad is diatonic to harmonic minor (Fmin in C harmonic minor); catalog it separately from the ii minor triad and note its pre-dominant function in minor-key cadences. [ch.1 pp.12-189]

---

## dim-triad

The diminished triad is the simplest expression of the leading-tone chord and functions transparently as a rootless G7 in C major. With only two catalog entries, it is the most lightly documented quality, but its substitution relationship to dom7 makes it a high-leverage item.

- **voicing-density-pairing** - The tritone between root and fifth is the structural core of the dim triad; Close voicings place the tritone between adjacent strings while Spread voicings distribute it - practice both to internalize the tritone's fingerboard geography. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
- **functional-voice-leading-substitution** - The dim triad on vii is a rootless G7 (containing the third and seventh of G7 without the root); cross-reference the dom7 catalog entries on the Functional layer and confirm that resolution targets are identical to the full G7. [ch.1 pp.12-189]
